summary: Return free glibc arena pages above a configurable reclamation threshold

replay.detail: Claim replay and projections are unchanged.

schema.detail: No database schema or schema version changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules, fleet coordination and admission are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No client, protocol or harness changes. The new worker runs only on Linux with glibc, using the same glibc runtime requirement as the existing allocator gauge.

downtime.detail: The daemon calls malloc_trim on a blocking thread when free arena bytes exceed the threshold. Arena locks can briefly pause allocator users, and reused discarded pages can cause page faults. The default check interval is 30 seconds and the default threshold is 256 MiB; these are reclamation triggers, not a latency or RSS bound.

manual.detail: No operator action is required for the defaults. Optional daemon environment settings ST3_MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_BYTES and ST3_MALLOC_TRIM_INTERVAL_SECS take effect after restart. A zero threshold disables the worker; invalid enabled-worker configuration fails startup.

recovery.detail: Trimming preserves live allocations and changes no durable state. Normal rollback remains available; an older build simply does not run this worker.
